claims.statement: The Commission states that EUDR applies from 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and from 30 June 2027 for most micro and small operators.
Covered commodities include cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soy, wood, and certain derived products; upstream suppliers may need to provide production locations.
Official implementation resources include an information system for submitting due-diligence statements and guidance on geolocation and traceability.

contrary_evidence: The EU amended the regulation in both 2024 and 2025, showing timing and administrative requirements are mutable.
Official systems already accept statements; a private clearinghouse must add supplier reuse and release-control value beyond submission.

economics.acquisition_route: Commodity-specific customs and compliance partners rather than broad outbound sales
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 350 importers averaging 18000 PLN annual revenue could create about 6.3m PLN revenue; at 25% operating margin and 75% ownership, retained cash and a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 6
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day for data and product, with commodity and legal expertise contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70-85% after geospatial processing, supplier support, secure storage, and expert escalation
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 12 SME importers at about 4000 PLN monthly could repay the pilot in 12-18 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 2000-8000 PLN monthly per importer plus 5-25 PLN per plot or shipment package
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every covered shipment repeats; supplier evidence can be reused and updated across participating importers

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned supplier-plot graph, document reuse, anomaly history, and integration at shipment release
fingerprint.customer: Polish and Central European importers of EUDR-covered commodities and products
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Commodity brokers, customs advisors, trade associations, and one narrow commodity pilot
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier portal, plot validation, document lineage, risk workflow, statement-reference tracking, and audit export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays subscription plus per supplier, plot, or shipment evidence package
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered shipment is prepared for EU placement, sale, or export and due diligence must be evidenced

founder_fit: Geospatial and entity-resolution work fits data science
Can start in one commodity with a software-led pilot
EU and Polish context provides a useful initial market
Channel partners can reduce high-frequency founder sales
risks: Regulatory dates and simplifications have already changed
Bad supplier evidence can expose the importer and platform to liability
Large trade-compliance suites can add EUDR modules

structure.commercial_archetype: Shipment compliance clearinghouse and supplier data network
structure.control_point: Reusable supplier-plot evidence identity embedded in an importer's shipment-release workflow
structure.critical_dependency: Non-EU suppliers must provide reliable geolocation and legality evidence and importers must accept shared records

thesis: Create a shared evidence workspace for Polish coffee, cocoa, wood, rubber, and related importers that binds supplier plots, legality documents, risk decisions, and due-diligence statement references to each incoming shipment. The control point is the reusable supplier-plot identity and the importer release gate, not one-off form filling.
title: EUDR Shipment Evidence Clearinghouse
uncertainties: Importer willingness to share supplier evidence in a common network
Actual Polish SME count and budget by commodity
How much verification responsibility customers expect the platform to assume
